name: Ayta Mag-Indi
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 5 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Green, Joanne. 1990. Phonological considerations in Ayta Mag-Indi. Unpublished manuscript, 10 pp. (dated 10 January 1990; fieldwork Pasbul, Porac 1987-88 and Nabuklod, Floridablanca 1989, Pampanga). SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 43451,https://www.sil.org/resources/archives/43451(scan posted CC BY-NC-SA).
catalog_locator: ms p. 3, sections 'Word: Definition' and 'STRESS', with footnote 5; stress also transcribed on every form in the phoneme-contrast lists ms pp. 6-9 and the illustrative text ms p. 10.
catalog_quote: A phonological word consists of a sequence of at least two syllables[5], one of which carries primary stress. In deliberate speech, these syllables occur together without a pause. Particles and pronouns do not carry primary stress and are therefore joined to preceding syllables to form a word. ... STRESS Word stress is not predictable and occurs on either the penultimate or ultimate syllable of a word. The following are minimal stress pairs: [qa'puq] 'granchild' ['qapuq] 'grandparent' [pa'kan] 'to feed someone else' ['pakan] 'however' [fn. 5: There are two exceptions: the deictics "di" and "du" which correspond to "dito" and "doon" in Tagalog.]
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is lexically contrastive within a two-syllable window at the right edge: every phonological word (minimally disyllabic) has one primary stress, which falls unpredictably on either the penult or the final syllable, as shown by segmentally identical minimal pairs; clitic particles and pronouns are unstressed and attach to the preceding word.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed; only primary stress is mentioned (one per phonological word).
new_statements.exceptions: Footnote: the deictics di and du are exceptions to the two-syllable minimum for a phonological word. Particles and pronouns never bear primary stress. Statements are restricted to the 'indigenous' phonological system; Kapampangan/Spanish loans are treated as a separate borrowed system. The 2013 factsheet notes phonemically long vowels (/daan/) exist but are not.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word including enclitic particles/pronouns; stress transcribed on citation forms throughout the contrast lists (e.g. ['mamut] 'sun' vs [ga'mit] 'hand', [bi'tis] 'foot', [kaliti'ptip] 'firefly', [mamakapa'tulaq]) and on running text (p. 9). Data from Pasbul (Porac) and Nabuklod (Floridablanca), Pampanga, 1987-1989.
new_statements.identity_note: Green 1990 describes Ayta Mag-Indi as spoken in Pasbul (Porac) and Nabuklod (Floridablanca), Pampanga = Glottolog magi1241 / ISO blx exactly (no dialect split in Glottolog). The author restricts her statements to the 'indigenous' stratum, treating Kapampangan/Spanish loans as a separate subsystem.

sources.note: Ms p.3 'STRESS': 'Word stress is not predictable and occurs on either the penultimate or ultimate syllable of a word', with minimal pairs [qa'puq] 'grandchild' / ['qapuq] 'grandparent', [pa'kan] 'to feed someone else' / ['pakan] 'however'; phonological word = at least two syllables one of which carries primary stress; particles and pronouns carry no primary stress and cliticise to the preceding word.
